newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Portugal hits out at "Club Med" label.
newsitem.headline: Portugal hits out at "Club Med" label.

text.p: Portuguese Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco lashed out on Monday at the "Club Med" label invented to discourage early membership of monetary union for Italy, Spain and Portugal and pledged that Lisbon would be ready to join the single currency from the start in 1999.
"Portugal is not even a Mediterranean country and France is indeed a Mediterranean country, so we are not in the 'Club Med'," Sousa Franco told Reuters Financial Television.

The "Club Med" tag, which some officials say originated in Germany, has become used widely to describe an assumption among many that if Italy does not qualify to join monetary union in 1999, Spain and Portugal will also have to be excluded.
Germany is believed to be very reluctant to allow Italy into monetary union at the start, fearing it would undermine the credibility of the new euro at its launch in January 1999.

Sousa Franco said he did not think European leaders would apply a "Club Med" approach when deciding which countries qualify for the single currency, "even if a part of public opinion is being induced to think like that".
"I do not think the decision about the single currency is going to be taken on geographical terms," he said.

Some officials have begun to discourage the use of the "Club Med" label which they say is a deliberate attempt to reduce the image of Italy, Spain and Portugal to the level of popular holiday destinations -- in other words not serious enough to join the euro currency club.
"The (Maastricht treaty) criteria will be the only basis for the judgement," Sousa Franco said.
He said Portugal planned to meet all the criteria "and that we will be on good terms to begin as a member of the single currency club on January 1, 1999."
"If we fulfil the criteria, of course we have the right to be in the first group of the single currency," he added.
Portugal believed it would be good for Europe if Spain and Italy also joined at the start. "But for us, it is no condition at all that Spain and Italy are first members."
"We will be judged according to our own mertis. Our economy is not dependent on the Spanish economy and even less on the Italian economy.
"We think we have a good case and it is only our single case, not the case of any other country," he added.
